CH-U01: format_output returns an output iterator that must be consumed. The display table uses <null>, CSV quotes coffee, beans as one field and writes None as an empty field, while JSONL preserves Unicode and JSON null. These representation choices do not mutate the source records and are not interchangeable null/type contracts.
CH-C01: Use an existing display format for people and CSV or JSONL under an explicit machine contract. Consume the returned iterator and join/write lines deliberately. CSV quoting preserves the comma field, while JSONL retains typed null and Unicode. A padded pretty table is not a lossless serializer, and selecting current formats does not require a library patch.
CH-P01: Select and validate ordered fields and types, define None versus empty text, and choose CSV or JSONL for machine consumers independently of display output. Consume the result iterator into the intended writer, validate/stage before publication if partial files are unacceptable, and handle failures explicitly. format_output can materialize rows and scan types, so one iterator return does not guarantee constant memory, complete business validation or transactions.
CH-D01: The JSON adapter builds dict(zip(headers,row,strict=True)), so equal id keys retain the last value; strict zip validates matching lengths rather than key uniqueness. CustomEncoder converts Decimal to float, which loses the supplied decimal digits. The pinned adapter does not have an existing duplicate_headers or decimal_mode option to claim.
CH-C02: Validate header uniqueness before export and reject or explicitly rename duplicate business fields under an application policy. When exact decimal text is required, pre-format Decimal with str and export it as a JSON string, making the type change explicit. That existing preprocessing boundary avoids a required library patch and does not pretend default numeric Decimal output is exact.
CH-D02: format_output retrieves formatter_args from the class-level registration and updates that same dictionary in place. A later new formatter instance still reaches the shared changed defaults, so the earlier per-call missing_value leaks. Reconstructing the object or changing rows does not isolate the registration mutation.
CH-M01: The real reference copies the registered top-level option mapping before applying this call's kwargs. Overrides still win for the current call, while built-in/custom registrations, different instances, deferred consumption and the registration caller dictionary remain isolated. Only the authorized implementation and public test file changed; no unrelated color, Decimal or one-shot-row behavior was bundled. Complete original regression and original-failing public tests were verified separately.
CH-C03: The outer list(data) retains row iterator objects, then _get_column_types consumes those rows before the formatter reads them again. For this known finite result set, materialize each row at an explicit bounded application boundary, then format the stable rows. Choose a maximum dataset/batch policy and account for the formatter's own materialization. This is a compatibility workaround, not a delivered library repair or a promise about infinite/end-to-end streaming input.
